parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Chagatai قوروغان (korugan), from the verb found in Turkish as قوریمق (korımak), korumak (“to protect, to shield”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قورولتای, قوریلتای, قورلتای, قرلتای, from Old Anatolian Turkish قرلتای (kurultay), from Mongolian хуралдай (xuraldaj), possibly via Chagatai; compare Russian курултай (kurultaj, “kurultai”). Surface analysis invites interpreting this as a compound kurul + -tay formed w

parole.significato: A formal way of addressing a person or people in a formal context or in a starting of a speech, letter, message, memo,…
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Chagatai سایین (sayın, “good, well, distinguished”), from a Mongolic language (compare modern Mongolian сайн (sajn, “good, well”)). Cognate with Persian صائین (sâ'in, toponym of a settlement in Iran).
